## Credit risk within risk management

## Reading a credit record and its notation

```{r step-001}
source("shared/formatting.R")
source("shared/figure-theme.R")
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r step-002}
records <- data.frame(
  loan_id = c(101, 102, 103, 104),
  exposure = c(1000, 2000, 1500, 3000),
  default = c(0, 1, 0, 0)
)
```

```{r step-003}
companion_kable(records, col.names = c("Loan ID", "Exposure ($)", "Default within one year"))
```

```{r step-004}
records$exposure
records[2, "exposure"]
records[2, ]
```

```{r step-005}
total_exposure <- sum(records$exposure)
observed_defaults <- sum(records$default)
number_of_loans <- nrow(records)
mean_exposure <- mean(records$exposure)
c(total_exposure = total_exposure,
  defaults = observed_defaults, mean_exposure = mean_exposure)
```

## Frequencies, probabilities, and the population at risk

### Keeping percentages and changes on the right scale

```{r step-006}
p_before <- 0.08
p_after <- 0.10
change_pp <- 100 * (p_after - p_before)
relative_change <- (p_after - p_before) / p_before
change_bps <- 10000 * (p_after - p_before)
c(percentage_points = change_pp,
  relative_change_percent = 100 * relative_change,
  basis_points = change_bps)
```

### Changing the denominator changes the question

```{r step-007}
segment_size <- c(A = 50, B = 50)
segment_defaults <- c(A = 2, B = 6)
segment_pd <- segment_defaults / segment_size
segment_weight <- segment_size / sum(segment_size)
overall_pd <- sum(segment_weight * segment_pd)
overall_pd
```

```{r step-008}
year1_pd <- 8 / 100
year2_conditional_pd <- 5 / 92
survival_two_years <- (1 - year1_pd) * (1 - year2_conditional_pd)
cumulative_two_year_pd <- 1 - survival_two_years
c(year2_conditional_pd = year2_conditional_pd,
  cumulative_two_year_pd = cumulative_two_year_pd)
```

### Learning a default probability from borrower information

The historical segment frequencies supply a simple fitted risk rule for new
applicants. Their segment is known at application; their future outcome is
still unknown. Chapter 1 estimates richer rules from several characteristics.

```{r foundations-segment-predictions}
new_applicant_segment <- c("A", "B", "B")
new_applicant_pd <- unname(segment_pd[new_applicant_segment])
new_applicant_pd
```

## Expected outcomes and dollar losses

```{r step-009}
pd <- 0.08
ead <- 10000
recovery <- 0.40
lgd <- 1 - recovery
loss_in_default <- ead * lgd
expected_loss <- pd * loss_in_default
c(loss_in_default = loss_in_default, expected_loss = expected_loss)
```

### Aggregating heterogeneous loans

```{r step-010}
loan_pd <- c(0.02, 0.06, 0.10)
loan_ead <- c(1000, 2000, 5000)
loan_lgd <- c(0.40, 0.40, 0.40)
loan_el <- loan_pd * loan_lgd * loan_ead
portfolio_el <- sum(loan_el)
loan_el
portfolio_el
```

```{r step-011}
exposure_weight <- loan_ead / sum(loan_ead)
weighted_pd <- sum(exposure_weight * loan_pd)
portfolio_el_check <- weighted_pd * 0.40 * sum(loan_ead)
c(weighted_pd = weighted_pd, expected_loss = portfolio_el_check)
```

## Distributions, dependence, and adverse outcomes

```{r step-012}
loss_values <- c(0, 5000, 10000)
prob_independent <- c(0.81, 0.18, 0.01)
prob_together <- c(0.90, 0, 0.10)
loss_distribution <- data.frame(
  loss = rep(loss_values, 2),
  probability = c(prob_independent, prob_together),
  dependence = rep(c("Independent", "Always together"), each = 3)
)
```

```{r step-013}
companion_kable(data.frame(
  "Portfolio loss ($)" = loss_values,
  "Independent" = fmt_pct(prob_independent, 0),
  "Always together" = fmt_pct(prob_together, 0),
  check.names = FALSE
))
```

```{r step-014}
loss_plot <- ggplot(loss_distribution,
  aes(x = factor(loss), y = probability)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, fill = "#0072B2") + facet_wrap(~ dependence)
```

```{r step-015}
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 3.2
loss_plot +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(probability, accuracy = 1)),
    vjust = -0.5, size = 3.3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), limits = c(0, 1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.03))) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("$0", "$5,000", "$10,000")) +
  labs(x = "Portfolio loss", y = "Probability") + book_figure_theme()
```

```{r step-016}
mean_independent <- sum(loss_values * prob_independent)
mean_together <- sum(loss_values * prob_together)
sd_independent <- sqrt(sum(prob_independent *
  (loss_values - mean_independent)^2))
sd_together <- sqrt(sum(prob_together *
  (loss_values - mean_together)^2))
round(c(mean_independent = mean_independent,
  mean_together = mean_together,
  sd_independent = sd_independent, sd_together = sd_together), 2)
```

### Reading a cumulative probability and a quantile

```{r step-017}
cdf_independent <- cumsum(prob_independent)
cdf_together <- cumsum(prob_together)
q95_independent <- loss_values[which(cdf_independent >= 0.95)[1]]
q95_together <- loss_values[which(cdf_together >= 0.95)[1]]
c(q95_independent = q95_independent, q95_together = q95_together)
```

### Simulating the same two-loan portfolio

Each vector position is a scenario for the same two loans. Independent uniform
draws give separate defaults; a shared default outcome makes both loans default
together. Each loan retains its supplied 10% PD in both models.

```{r foundations-simulation}
set.seed(20261014)
n_scenarios <- 10000
draw_1 <- runif(n_scenarios)
draw_2 <- runif(n_scenarios)
default_1 <- draw_1 < 0.10
default_2 <- draw_2 < 0.10
sim_loss_independent <- 5000 * (default_1 + default_2)
sim_loss_together <- 10000 * default_1
simulation_example <- which(default_1 & default_2)[1]
c(scenario = simulation_example,
  draw_1 = draw_1[simulation_example],
  draw_2 = draw_2[simulation_example],
  loss = sim_loss_independent[simulation_example])
```

```{r foundations-simulation-check}
simulation_check <- data.frame(
  dependence = c("Independent", "Always together"),
  exact_mean_loss = c(mean_independent, mean_together),
  simulated_mean_loss = c(mean(sim_loss_independent),
    mean(sim_loss_together)),
  exact_joint_pd = c(0.10^2, 0.10),
  simulated_joint_pd = c(mean(default_1 & default_2),
    mean(default_1))
)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Dependence = simulation_check$dependence,
  `Exact mean ($)` = fmt_num(simulation_check$exact_mean_loss, 2),
  `Simulated mean ($)` = fmt_num(simulation_check$simulated_mean_loss, 2),
  `Exact joint PD` = fmt_pct(simulation_check$exact_joint_pd, 2),
  `Simulated joint PD` = fmt_pct(simulation_check$simulated_joint_pd, 2),
  check.names = FALSE
))
```

Simulation approximates the consequences of supplied credit assumptions.
Larger runs reduce Monte Carlo variability; borrower-risk evidence is needed
separately to choose those assumptions.

## Standardized scores, logarithms, and probabilities

```{r step-018}
normal_pd <- 0.08
normal_threshold <- qnorm(normal_pd)
normal_check <- pnorm(normal_threshold)
central_probability <- pnorm(1) - pnorm(-1)
c(threshold = normal_threshold, recovered_pd = normal_check,
  probability_between_minus1_and_1 = central_probability)
```

```{r step-019}
normal_grid <- data.frame(z = seq(-3.5, 3.5, length.out = 701))
normal_grid$density <- dnorm(normal_grid$z)
normal_plot <- ggplot(normal_grid, aes(z, density)) + geom_line()
```

```{r step-020}
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 3.3
normal_tail <- data.frame(z = seq(-3.5, normal_threshold, length.out = 300))
normal_tail$density <- dnorm(normal_tail$z)
normal_plot +
  geom_area(data = normal_tail, fill = "#B22222", alpha = 0.65) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, color = "#0072B2") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = normal_threshold, linetype = "dotted",
    linewidth = 0.35, color = "#B22222") +
  annotate("text", x = -2.2, y = 0.25,
    label = "Left-tail probability\n8%", size = 3.2) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.44), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  labs(x = "Standardized score", y = "Density") + book_figure_theme()
```

### Moving between a probability and a model score

```{r step-021}
probability <- 0.08
odds <- probability / (1 - probability)
score <- log(odds)
probability_check <- 1 / (1 + exp(-score))
c(odds = odds, score = score, recovered_pd = probability_check)
```

## Time, interest, and present value

```{r step-022}
annual_rate <- 0.05
initial_amount <- 1000
years <- 2
future_amount <- initial_amount * (1 + annual_rate)^years
present_value_check <- future_amount / (1 + annual_rate)^years
c(future_amount = future_amount, present_value = present_value_check)
```

```{r step-023}
payment_time <- c(1, 2)
cash_flow <- c(50, 1050)
discount_factor <- (1 + annual_rate)^(-payment_time)
payment_pv <- cash_flow * discount_factor
sum(payment_pv)
```

### Recognizing an equivalent exponential convention

```{r step-024}
continuous_rate <- log(1 + annual_rate)
discount_discrete <- (1 + annual_rate)^(-years)
discount_exponential <- exp(-continuous_rate * years)
c(continuous_rate = continuous_rate,
  discrete_factor = discount_discrete,
  exponential_factor = discount_exponential)
```

### A default probability implied by a bond price

The constructed example assumes an observed one-year bond price of exactly
94/1.05, a promised payment of 100 and recovery of 40 at maturity. Calibrate
the default pricing probability using the effective risk-free rate of 5%.
Repricing the input bond verifies the calibration; it is not independent
evidence of cheapness or a real-world default-frequency estimate.

```{r foundations-bond-calibration}
bond_face <- 100
bond_recovery <- 40
bond_rf <- 0.05
bond_price <- 94 / (1 + bond_rf)
bond_q <- (bond_face - bond_price * (1 + bond_rf)) /
  (bond_face - bond_recovery)
bond_expected_payment <- (1 - bond_q) * bond_face + bond_q * bond_recovery
bond_repriced <- bond_expected_payment / (1 + bond_rf)
round(c(price = bond_price, default_probability = bond_q,
        expected_payment = bond_expected_payment,
        repriced_bond = bond_repriced), 4)
```

### Using the same states to value default protection

Protection pays 60 if this same bond defaults and zero otherwise, at the same
one-year maturity and without counterparty risk. Bond plus protection pays
100 in both states. Frictionless trading and short selling imply that its
price equals the risk-free bond price. The two methods below must agree.

```{r foundations-default-protection}
bond_risk_free_price <- bond_face / (1 + bond_rf)
protection_payment <- bond_face - bond_recovery
protection_from_prices <- bond_risk_free_price - bond_price
protection_from_q <- protection_payment * bond_q / (1 + bond_rf)
round(c(risk_free_bond = bond_risk_free_price,
        risky_bond = bond_price,
        protection_from_prices = protection_from_prices,
        protection_from_q = protection_from_q), 4)
```

## Sampling uncertainty, assumptions, and scenarios

```{r step-025}
estimated_pd <- 0.08
sample_sizes <- c(100, 10000)
standard_errors <- sqrt(estimated_pd * (1 - estimated_pd) / sample_sizes)
100 * standard_errors
```

### Reading a result conditional on a scenario

```{r step-026}
scenario_pd <- c(Baseline = 0.08, Stress = 0.12)
scenario_el <- scenario_pd * 10000 * 0.60
scenario_el
unname(scenario_el["Stress"] - scenario_el["Baseline"])
```

Conditioning a PD on economic conditions specifies a scenario. It does not
automatically turn that PD into a risk-neutral pricing probability. Identify
the probability's interpretation before using it for forecasting or valuation.
